guardrails.no_p_hacking: Each is registered ONCE with fixed parameters before running. Failures are reported and the variant dropped; no parameter sweeps.
guardrails.multiple_testing_disclosure: These are the 11th-13th variants on the same data. Accumulated searching is itself a statistical cost: the more variants tried, the more likely one looks good by luck. Treat any single winner with more suspicion than the first result, and confirm on real-option data before promoting anything.
guardrails.same_deviations: Proxied IV, constant-IV repricing, model credit -> UPPER BOUND.

trial_accounting.note: same universe/structures; these are policy refinements, but see the multiple-testing disclosure.

promotion: No promotion. SHADOW research. v5 stays live; v10 remains the leading candidate unless one of these clearly beats it.
objective: STRUCTURE DESIGN lever (never tested in the ETF lane): replace the iron condor with a NO-UPSIDE-RISK condor (jade-lizard principle) for neutral leans -- require total credit >= the call-side width so the call wing is fully financed and the structure cannot lose to the upside.
philosophy: Every failure mode we have found on the call side is upside risk in a market with positive drift (calls -$913 in v5; SMH/GLD/QQQ ran through short strikes). Instead of predicting when NOT to sell calls (v9 failed, v10 half-worked), remove upside risk BY CONSTRUCTION. The SPY lane already uses this invariant for its jade lizard; the ETF lane never adopted it.
change: For neutral (iron condor) entries, require total_credit >= call_width; if the structure cannot meet it, skip the trade. Defined risk on the put side is retained (the $1,000 cap forbids a naked put). Directional structures unchanged from v10.
predictions: condor trade count falls (many will not clear the financing requirement)
the surviving condors have NO upside losses -- all condor losses are downside
2022 (a downside year) is not improved; the benefit should appear in strong up-years (2021, 2024)
total PnL direction uncertain: fewer trades, but no upside tail
risk: Requiring credit >= call width is restrictive; if too few condors qualify the book loses its main profit engine (condors were +$9,729 of v5's PnL).
